statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107817 is MariaDB advisory GHSA-89ph-64cf-gqcc: https://github.com/MariaDB/server/security/advisories/GHSA-89ph-64cf-gqcc . The mysql_json plugin, which reads MySQL binary JSON from imported MySQL tables, trusted the offsets and lengths stored in that data, so a crafted table could cause out-of-bounds reads, information disclosure or a server crash. MariaDB fixed it in 11.8.9 (and 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 12.3.3 and 13.0.2) with commit https://github.com/MariaDB/server/commit/851f52470d470a96a66e0b7e5599f3b6c2e45907 (MDEV-40678), which in plugin/type_mysql_json/mysql_json.cc rejects a value offset at or past the end of the data in parse_mysql_scalar_or_value and a key that extends past the end of the object in parse_array_or_object. Debian's mariadb 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 does not include it. DHI backports that commit unmodified, and the fixed version is the first build that carries it. We compared all four published builds of 1:11.8.6-0+deb13u1 on amd64 and arm64, reading function symbols from the matching -dbgsym packages. In type_mysql_json.so from the mariadb-server package, parse_mysql_scalar_or_value grows from 109 to 151 bytes and parse_array_or_object from 1004 to 1036 bytes on amd64 (100 to 120 and 884 to 912 bytes on arm64) between the build before the fix and the fixed build. The two later builds ship the same type_mysql_json.so as the fixed build (identical build ID) on both architectures. The fixed build's mariadb-test-data package also carries the upstream MDEV-40678 regression test, and its changelog lists this CVE.
